newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas rises with cold forecast, NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas rises with cold forecast, NYMEX.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices gained an average of 10 cents Monday, propped up by colder temperatures forecast for most of the U.S. later this week and a rallying futures market, industry sources said.
Gulf Coast gas traded more than 10 cents higher into the mid-$2.80s to low-$2.90s, as forecasters called for a return to below-normal temperatures in the Northeast by Thursday.
NYMEX's December Henry Hub contract, set to expire Thursday, soared to a new high of $3.01 in early Monday trading.
In the New York market, prices bounced back into the $3.45-3.55 area, up about 10 cents from Friday, as buyers turned to the spot market to meet heating demand.
Temperatures in the Northeast are expected to dip to five to 10 degrees below-normal on Thursday and Friday, which should result in a greater volume of storage withdrawals.
Baltimore Gas and Electric said Monday that its 850 megawatt Calvert Cliffs nuclear unit 2, shut this weekend, would restart Tuesday.
In the Midcontinent, a strong heating demand pushed prices about 10 cents higher to the $2.70 area.
At the Chicago city-gate, traders reported closing deals in the $3.10 area.
Similarly in south Texas, prices rose by five to 10 cents to the high-$2.60s to mid-$2.70s.
A cold front is anticipated for the Gulf Coast area later this week and into the weekend.
In west Texas, Permian prices rose by about seven cents to the high-$2.50s to low-$2.60s, with Waha quoted in the mid-$2.60s.

West Coast demand continued to be strong as Canadian exports were scarce due to the severely cold weather in Alberta. As a result, prices at the southern California border gained an additional three cents today to the low-to-mid $2.70s.
